Wantage CE Primary School
Welcome to Wantage CE Primary School, an Ofsted 'Good' school situated in the South Oxfordshire market town of Wantage. I am so proud of this wonderful community of learners and I would like to thank you for taking the time to find out more about us. As you learn about who we are and what we are like as a school - a school where everyone learns, is inspired, flourishes and enjoys life in all its fullness - my hope is that you will see our school vision shining through… click on the link below to find out more.
Mr A. Browne - Headteacher
Our Church School
'Life in Abundance' John 10:10
Our church links with Wantage Parish Church of Saints Peter & Paul are very important to us. A team from church present a weekly Open the Book assembly and Katherine (our local vicar) regularly joins us for collective worship. We attend church each term and we look forward to the Prayer Space team who visit us twice a year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wantage CE Primary School - Brilliant Ofsted Report
pageCache.text:
Brilliant Ofsted Report
.Wantage CE Primary School continues to be a good school!!!
We are delighted with the outcome of our Ofsted inspection which took place last term.
The type of inspection that we received is known as an ungraded inspection, which means that we were inspected to make sure that we continue to be a good school. I am very pleased to say that the outcome of the inspection is that: ‘Wantage Church of England Primary School has taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at the previous inspection’.
Please take the time to read through the report. I am sure that you will agree that the report is full of lovely statements which describe our school very well. I am particularly pleased that ‘pupils enjoy learning’ here, that ‘teachers make lessons fun and bring learning to life’ and that ‘pupils feel happy and safe’. I love that we have created ‘a nurturing and caring environment for all’ and that pupils say we are ‘a kind school, where you can be yourself’.
There is so much more that I would like to quote and highlight for you, so please do read the report in its entirety.
I would like to thank everyone associated with Wantage CE Primary School for all that they do to create such a wonderful school. I am proud to be part of this community and humbled to be headteacher to such super staff, pupils and families. I am also grateful to our governors and colleagues from the trust who support us so well.

Curriculum Enrichment
Trips and Visits
Learning doesn’t just happen in the classroom at Wantage CE.
We offer a wide range of enrichment activities to every year group in the school.
Trip to Roves Farm
Trip to Hill End
Visits to Wantage Library
Trip to Oxford Castle
Trip to Beale Park
Trip to the Cotswold Wildlife Park
Trip to Pizza Express to make pizza!
1 night residential to Court Hill
Trip to The Living Rainforest
Trip to Harwell Science Exhibition
Year 5 Easter Passion Play
4 night residential to Kilvrough (South Wales)
Visit from the Royal Marines - Technology
Year 6 Summer Performance
Clubs
We are delighted to be able to offer a wide range of before/after-school clubs. Please ask at the school office for the current list.
These generally include: judo, rugby, netball, tennis, frisbee, water-polo, tri-golf and ‘quad kids’ athletics, and we compete in a range of fixtures both in and outside of school.
We are very proud of our sporting successes and the ever-increasing percentage of children who take part in a wide range of sports, leading us to achieve the Schools Games Gold Award this year.
We compete in local and national Maths competitions against other schools and run a Robotics and Coding Club for Years 5 and 6. With regard to music, we offer orchestra and choir, and a Recorder Club. We can also help facilitate Musical Instrument lessons - strings, woodwind, keyboard, guitar and drums.
Previously we have also offered Cooking, Gardening, Science and Art Clubs.
Last year, pupils from Wantage CE Primary school experienced trips to the Vale and Downland Museum, Kilvrough Outdoor Education Centre, Court Hill Outdoor Centre, Oxford Castle, Wantage Library, The Bristol Sea Life Centre, Roves Farm, Hill End Outdoor Centre, Millets Farm, Winchester Science Museum and The Planetarium.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wantage CE Primary School - Opening Hours
pageCache.text:
Opening Hours
Our gates are opened in the morning at 8:30am when children and families are welcome to come onto the school site and wait on the playground for the start of the school day.
We do ask you to remain with your children until the classroom doors are opened and you have handed your child over to their teacher.
The school day starts at 8:40am when children are greeted by their teacher and can enter their classrooms.
The school day ends at 3:15pm.
You are welcome to wait on the playground to collect your child when the school gates are reopened at 3:10pm.
The School Day
The school day starts at 8:40am
There is a 15 minute break between 10:40am and 10:55am
Lunch is approximately 12:00pm to 12:55pm (some younger classes start and finish their lunch break earlier than older classes)
The school day finishes at 3:15pm
This is equal to 6 hours 35 minutes a day, or 32 hours 55 minutes a week.

Young Carers
At Wantage CE Primary School we are aware that some of our pupils are young carers.
A young carer is someone under 18 who is caring for a family member, sibling or friend who is ill, frail, disabled or has mental health or addiction problems. They often take on a practical and/or emotional caring responsibilities that would normally be expected of an adult.
We know that young carers may need a little extra support to enjoy and do well at school. At Wantage CE Primary School we are committed to ensuring that all pupils who are young carers are identified and supported effectively.
If you feel your child may be a Young Carer, please contact the school office.

Governors
The Local Governing Committee (LGC) of the school consists of nine governors representing parents, the church, staff and the community.
As part of the Cambrian Learning Trust (CLT), the LGC operates under a Scheme of Delegation from the Board of the Trust and the CLT Board is responsible for appointing three members of the LGC. Two members of the LGC are Foundation Governors, appointed by the Diocese of Oxford. Two governors act as representatives of the parent body, the staff are represented by one staff governor and the Headteacher is an officer of the committee, not a governor.
The Role of the LGC
The governors’ key role is to support and challenge the Headteacher and staff in their management of the school to ensure that we are delivering the very best education to the children. We promote the provision of a secure, friendly learning environment, high-quality teaching and breadth of opportunity, allowing every child to be happy at school and to flourish and reach their full potential.
Governors also contribute to the school’s development plan and have a role in overseeing the financial management of the school. The LGC meets formally six times per year, with occasional additional meetings as required. Members of the LGC take responsibility for supporting and monitoring various aspects of the life of the school that have been highlighted in the school’s development plan as well as key management areas, such as Safeguarding and Finance.
The CLT recognises that it is essential for governors to be well-informed and regular Governor Development evenings are arranged so that governors from all the Trust schools get together for discussion and workshops. As well as providing necessary updates and training, these offer opportunities for sharing ideas and best practice. In addition, the Chairs of Governors meet several times during the year. Members of the CLTCentral Team are always willing to help and advise the LGC in its work.
If you have any questions about the governing body or are interested in becoming a governor, please contact us via the school office.
Barry Cook and Abi Drewitt - Chairs of Governors
Abigail Drewitt (Vice Chair and Director Appointed Governor)
I have been a board appointed governor since 2021, taking up the role of co-vice chair in 2023 alongside Barry Cook.
I have a wealth of experience in the education sector and I am currently on the leadership team at The Marlborough C of E School Woodstock, with responsibilities for student engagement and personal development. I am passionate about helping to ensure the best possible outcomes for all pupils in the classroom and beyond.
I have a young son and when I'm not spending time with family and friends, I enjoy running and taking part in a variety of sports.
Sarah Gniadek-Pitt (Diocesan Governor)
The Revd Katherine Price (Diocesan Governor)
I am the Vicar of Wantage. I moved to Wantage in 2022 from Oxford, where I was previously a College Chaplain. I visit the school regularly to lead Collective Worship, and I am the lead governor for the school’s Christian ethos. I'm also the mother of a child starting at the school in 2023!
Caroline Haines (Director Appointed Governor)
I have lived in this area for 17 years and I became a Governor this year. I was a teacher for 33 years before I retired a few years ago. I have taught in various counties and my areas of specialism are Primary, SEND and Music. I worked for ten years at Hampshire Music Service. I believe all children should have opportunities to help them reach their full potential and I’m also keen to promote the arts in school to help them achieve that. Music is still a big part of my life. I play piano, have just started learning the organ and I sing in the parish church choir. This year I have enjoyed welcoming several children from school to our choir. I enjoy helping regularly in assemblies with the Open the Book team and listening to readers. You may see me locally out and about, walking my two dogs, a greyhound and King Charles spaniel.
Sheila Apps (Director Appointed Governor)
Kirsty Taylor (Parent Governor)
Kirsty was appointed in July 2024. She is parent to a pupil in Year 1.
Katie Chalmers (Staff Governor)
Lucy Crick (Parent Governor)
Lucy was appointed in March 2026. She is parent to pupils in Year 2 and Year 4.
